status_when_frozen: No window listed here had been run or analysed. All hypotheses, thresholds and decision rules below were fixed from the exploratory replay of the 15 runs of 12 October 2026 (single 48-h window, live orbital elements), which is reported separately as exploratory.
unit_of_analysis: analysis window (one 48-h window per run); onsets and cloud realisations are nested within it

settings.h1_floor_margin: one orbital period at the fleet's median altitude

hypotheses.H1a: Latency non-inferiority of the earliest-completion cover (ECC, k = 30): in a window, the share of evaluable onsets at which ECC reaches 95% of the tiles reachable in the onset's 24-h horizon no later than one orbital period after the physical floor (clear sky). Claim: the mean of this share over windows is at least 90%.
hypotheses.H1b: Image economy of ECC: in a window, the share of eligible onsets (first-come-first-served needs two or more images to reach the level) at which ECC meets the H1a criterion with fewer images than first-come-first-served. Claim: the mean of this share over windows is at least 90%.
hypotheses.H2: Value of acting on cloud observations: in a window, the mean over 20 cloud realisations (correlated model, L = 50 km, T = 3 h, p = 0.35) of the coverage difference, adaptive selector minus the same planner run in advance without observations, both with the same number of images (time-aware objective). Claim: the mean of this difference over windows is above 0.

evaluability.rule_onsets: a window counts for H1a/H1b only with at least 29 evaluated (resp. eligible) onsets
evaluability.rule_h2: a window counts for H2 only when H2 is evaluable in it (the selector adapted at least once and the greedy given the cloud beats the open-loop plan in some realisation)

decision_rules.H1a_H1b: SUPPORTED if the one-sided (1 - alpha') Student-t lower confidence bound of the mean over evaluable windows is >= 90%; NOT SUPPORTED otherwise; NOT EVALUABLE with fewer than 5 evaluable windows
decision_rules.H2: SUPPORTED if the one-sided (1 - alpha') Student-t lower confidence bound of the mean over evaluable windows is > 0 coverage points; NOT SUPPORTED otherwise; NOT EVALUABLE with fewer than 5 evaluable windows
decision_rules.alpha_prime: alpha / 3 (Bonferroni over the three primary hypotheses) for the primary design; alpha for secondary designs, which are exploratory

deviations_policy: Any change to code, settings, windows or rules after freezing is reported as a deviation with its reason; results under the frozen plan are reported regardless.

amendments.reason: Points a referee is expected to raise. (1) H1a is met at every onset with the protocol's budget of 30 images because earliest-completion cover (ECC) searches from the physical floor, so H1a shows that the budget suffices; smaller budgets show where it starts to bind. (2) The archive validation (Cell 7D) recorded near-zero scene cloud cover in these dry-season windows, against the protocol's constant cloud probability of 0.35; the per-tile climatology option of the release shows H2 under a realistic probability. (3) H1b failed in one window (14 September) through ties with first-come-first-served; the exact minimum number of images at each onset shows whether any selector could have used fewer. (4) The exact optimum was measured on 6-h sub-problems only; one full-window instance per window measures ECC's greedy cover against the exact minimum at full scale and repeats the confirmatory run otherwise (determinism check).

amendments.question: What sets the physical floor: the wait for the first usable pass, the coverage geometry, or delivery?
amendments.method: Each onset's floor (95% of reachable cells, clear sky, 24-h horizon) split exactly into W (onset to the first acquisition with a usable cell), G (that acquisition to the acquisition of the pass that completes the level) and L (acquisition to delivery of that pass); sun elevation at the region's centroid at the onset from the pipeline's NOAA routine. Every floor and reachable count is recomputed from arf_refined_events.csv and must equal arf_onset_robustness.csv, or the script stops.

amendments.status_when_amended: POST HOC. Written after the confirmatory results and A4 to A11 were read, to bound the first limitation (every daylight PlanetScope pass assumed to acquire). While the script was tested, it was run on the window of 3 August 2026 (sandbox copy of that run, 20 seeds): H1a share 100% at every fraction; H1b share 100, 96.5, 84.0 and 52.9% at f = 1, 0.75, 0.5 and 0.25; median floor unchanged at 12.1 h. No other window has been replayed.
amendments.question: How do the floor, the reachable share and the H1a and H1b shares change if only a fraction f of PlanetScope's predicted daylight passes acquire an image?
amendments.method: A PlanetScope pass is a maximal run of consecutive minutes of one FLOCK satellite. Per seed (1 to 20) each pass gets one uniform draw u and acquires when u < f (nested fractions f = 1, 0.75, 0.5, 0.25); Sentinel-2 and Landsat passes are always kept. Per onset, the floor, reachable count, ECC (k = 30) and FCFS image count are recomputed with the rules of Cell 7C; at f = 1 every onset must equal the run's arf_onset_robustness.csv (floor, reachable, ECC time, ECC images, FCFS images), or the script stops. H1a and H1b shares by the protocol's rules, margin = the run's t_max_wait_min.
amendments.scope: Read-only replay of the 8 primary dry-season windows (3 Aug to 21 Sep 2026) and the 8 wet-season windows of A5 (5 Jan to 23 Feb 2026, p = 0.35 runs). Descriptive sensitivity analysis; no hypothesis, no decision changes. It bounds the acquisition assumption from the model side; it does not measure Planet's acquisition fraction, which needs catalogue metadata.

No other window has been replayed.
amendments.question: How does ECC compare with published image selectors given exactly the same candidates: the run's predicted events of the 24 h after each onset, clear sky, H3 resolution 7, 95% of the reachable cells?
amendments.method: Three selectors re-implemented from their published descriptions, adapted to predicted passes measured from the onset: WANG26 (Wang et al. 2026, Remote Sensing 18(11):1855, sections 3.3 to 3.5: rank by time, resolution, cloud; accept an image that intersects the remaining target; remove invalid coverage; earliest delivery after the onset stands for 'most recent'), reported stopped at the level and run to full coverage; KS17 (Kempeneers and Soille 2017, Big Earth Data 1(1-2):145-158: per tile, minimum set of at most 5 images maximising covered cells by Sequential Floating Forward Search; tile = H3 resolution-3 parent; the SFFS body is the standard one of Pudil et al. 1994, an assumption, because the article's steps were not available to us); PAN24 (Pan et al. 2024, Geo-spatial Information Science 27(5):1524-1541: shortest span of delivery times after the onset whose images reach the level, ties to the earliest span, then the images of that span by largest new coverage; HFA-Net quality grading has no counterpart for predicted passes and is not used). Per onset: time to the level, images, coverage reached. The floor, ECC and FCFS are recomputed with the A13 port of Cell 7C and must equal the run's arf_onset_robustness.csv, or the script stops.
amendments.scope: Read-only replay of the 8 primary dry-season windows (3 Aug to 21 Sep 2026) and the 8 wet-season windows of A5 (5 Jan to 23 Feb 2026, p = 0.35 runs), and of the A15 windows once run. Descriptive; no hypothesis, no decision changes.

amendments.status_when_amended: REGISTERED REPLICATION, POST HOC IN MOTIVATION. Written after the confirmatory results and A4 to A13 were read (H1b was decided by one of eight windows), and before any run of the windows below existed.
amendments.question: Do H1a, H1b and H2 hold in eight further windows of the 2026 dry season?
amendments.reason: The dry season over the region runs from May to October, with dryland fire activity peaking in September (Heinl et al. 2007) and the Okavango flood at its maximum extent in July to September (Inman and Lyons 2020). The added windows extend the confirmatory windows (3 August to 21 September) to July and to late September and October. The same weeks of 2025 are not used: the pipeline builds the fleet from the current CelesTrak lists, so satellites retired since 2025 would drop out.
amendments.method: Release 1.5.3 unchanged, primary design (CKGR + Okavango, earth-resources+planet, conservative swath, p = 0.35), run retrospectively with Space-Track gp_history element sets; runner arf_dryext_runner_a15.py (the A5 runner with these windows and the p = 0.35 setting only).
amendments.decision_rules: H1a, H1b and H2 are decided on these eight windows alone, by the protocol's decision_rules: one-sided Student-t lower bound of the mean over windows at alpha/3 at least threshold_pct (H1a, H1b) or above 0 (H2); a window counts with at least min_evaluable_onsets evaluable onsets; a hypothesis is decided only with at least 5 windows. The original confirmatory decisions are not changed. Over all sixteen dry-season windows the statistics are reported descriptively, with no decision.
amendments.scope: Adds eight runs. Decisions reported as a registered replication beside the confirmatory decisions.

amendments.status_when_amended: POST HOC. Written after the confirmatory results and A4 to A13 were read. Part a was tested on the window of 3 August 2026 (sandbox copy of that run): ECC stayed within the H1a margin of the floor at every onset in every scenario; the median floor rose from 12.1 h to 13.8 h (fast), 15.3 h (typical) and 36.1 h (slow). Part b was tested only on synthetic quality bands; no real Landsat scene has been read.
amendments.question: (a) How do the floor, ECC and FCFS change when real product latencies are added to delivery? (b) How cloudy were the Landsat 8 and 9 acquisitions of the primary windows?
amendments.method: (a) Per-mission latency added to every delivery time; scenarios (Sentinel-2, Landsat, PlanetScope, hours): fast 1.67, 4, 2; typical 3, 6, 6; slow 24, 12, 24; and PlanetScope 2, 6, 12 or 24 with Sentinel-2 3 and Landsat 6. Sources: ESA Sentinel-2 MSI Technical Guide timeliness (Real-Time no later than 100 min; Near Real-Time 100 min to 3 h; Nominal 3 to 24 h); USGS Landsat Collection 2 Level-1 (Real-Time 4 to 6 h, under 12 h). No published PlanetScope latency was found: its values are scenarios. Recomputed with the registered A13 port; identity with arf_onset_robustness.csv at zero latency, or the script stops. (b) Landsat 8/9 Collection 2 Level-2 QA_PIXEL (USGS LSDS-1619 v6.0, Table 6-2) read from Microsoft Planetary Computer (collection landsat-c2-l2, anonymous signing), sampled at the 7 points per tile of A8; a point is cloudy when bit 1, 3 or 4 is set (sensitivity: or bit 2); the tile and overpass rules of A8.
amendments.scope: (a) Read-only replay of the 8 primary dry-season windows (3 Aug to 21 Sep 2026) and the 8 wet-season windows of A5 (5 Jan to 23 Feb 2026, p = 0.35 runs) and of the A15 windows once run. (b) The same windows. Descriptive; no hypothesis, no decision changes. PlanetScope cloud (UDM2) is not measured: it needs a Planet licence.

amendments.status_when_amended: EXPLORATORY, REGISTERED BEFORE ANY OF ITS RUNS. Written after the confirmatory results and A4 to A16 were registered, and after the 26 runs of the dense arm of A3 (release 1.5.4), which are superseded and not reported: they gave every Starlink satellite an off-nadir half-angle of 9.22 deg that has no source (a ground swath of about 155 to 180 km). The scripts were tested on synthetic Starlink-like orbits only (N = 5, 20 and 100 with real Orekit, window of 3 August 2026); no result has been seen.
amendments.question: How do the earliest-completion floor, the reachable share of the region and the image economy of ECC change with the size N of a dense Earth-observation constellation, and beyond which N does the floor stop falling? (Objectives O1 to O4 of the proposal at the densities it names, N = 5, 20 and 100, and beyond.)

design.geometry: Starlink satellites operational at each window start (Space-Track gp_history), one seeded random order per window, nested fleets (the first N)
design.assumed_camera: nadir, ground swath proxy_swath_km; imaging only with the Sun at least proxy_min_sun_elev_deg above the imaged point; primary 32.5 km (PlanetScope SuperDove frame width, ESA Earth Online, accessed 4 Nov 2026) and 10 deg (Planet's constraint for the Doves, cited in Paper 1)
design.region_and_windows: CKGR + Okavango; the eight protocol windows (3 August to 21 September 2026)
design.settings: every protocol setting, cloud-sensitivity sweep off
design.core: 32.5 km, 10 deg; N = 5, 20, 100, 250, 500, 1000, 2000 in all eight windows; N = 4000 in the windows of 3 August and 7 September

amendments.analysis: Descriptive; no hypothesis decision. Per run: the medians over onsets of the floor to 95% of the reachable cells and of the reachable share; the share of onsets covering 95% of the whole region; ECC and FCFS images; H1a- and H1b-type shares; the Fail-Signal gain. Means over windows with window-block bootstrap 95% intervals (B = 2000, seed 42). Saturation of the core floor against N, three ways, each with window-block bootstrap intervals: T(N) = T_inf + a N^-b with N* = (a/m)^(1/b) and the smallest grid N within m of T_inf, for m = 0.5 h and 1 h; a one-breakpoint segmented regression on log10 N (Muggeo 2003); the Kneedle knee (Satopaa et al. 2011).
amendments.scope: New runs only, in folders tagged _sun<deg>_sw<km>km that no earlier run uses; real-fleet results and decisions unchanged. Reported in Paper 2 as an exploratory study on an assumed instrument.

amendments.status_when_amended: CORRECTION OF A17'S RELEASE, REGISTERED BEFORE ANY OF ITS CORE OR SENSITIVITY RUNS. Only the A17 smoke stage had run (release 1.5.5; N = 5 and 20, window of 3 August 2026, 10 November 2026). Its log reported 104 of 10,881 Starlink element sets as malformed. A read-only check of the cached Space-Track files, with the parsing steps of 1.5.5, found every rejected record to carry an Alpha-5 catalogue number, and the number rising with the window: 104, 152, 176, 229, 309, 365, 418 and 424 of 10,881 to 11,135 records (3 August to 21 September 2026). The two smoke runs are superseded and not reported; their folders are kept. No other A17 run exists.
amendments.reason: Catalogue numbers of 100000 and above are written in the 5-character TLE field as Alpha-5: a leading capital letter, A = 10 to Z = 33 with I and O omitted, so that 339999 => Z9999 (Space-Track documentation, section Alpha-5, read 10 November 2026). Release 1.5.5 read the field as an integer, so every Starlink satellite catalogued since number 100000 was reached was rejected, and the samples were drawn from the older satellites only, a bias that grows across the eight windows.
amendments.change: Release 1.5.6 decodes Alpha-5 in the operational filter and in the pin file (Cell 2) and names its pin files _opsample_a5 so that no 1.5.5 pin is reused. Nothing else changes; Orekit 13.1.9 already decodes Alpha-5 in TLE(line1, line2). Real fleets are unaffected: their catalogue numbers come from the OMM field NORAD_CAT_ID, not from the TLE line, in release 1.5.3 as in 1.5.6.
amendments.checks: Sandbox, no network: the decoding agrees with Space-Track's examples and, for all 24 letters, with Orekit's own decoding of checksummed lines; on synthetic Starlink-like element sets numbered from 99000 (9,085 of 10,084 Alpha-5), 1.5.5 rejects all 9,085 and 1.5.6 none, the two select identically on 5-digit records, and Cells 0 to 9 of 1.5.6 run without error at N = 20 and 100 with 16 of 20 and 88 of 100 Alpha-5 satellites in the fleet.
amendments.design: A17's design, analysis and scope unchanged in every other respect: release 1.5.6 (SHA-256 240698a9c52c6f4a17bf16ae489fdea5cba721e0ec0795a9973c1a368b2532b3) in place of 1.5.5; batches paper2_v156_a18_smoke, paper2_v156_a18_core and paper2_v156_a18_sens; summary written to ARF_batch/paper2_a18. Where a 1.5.5 smoke folder already holds a complete run, 1.5.6 writes to the same name with the suffix _v156 (Cell 0 rule since 1.5.2).

amendments.status_when_amended: POST HOC. Registered AFTER the 88 runs of A17/A18 (release 1.5.6; 58 core, 30 sensitivity, all done, 10 to 15 November 2026) and after their summary had been read. Nothing of A19 had been run when it was registered. Every A19 result is to be labelled post hoc.
amendments.what_was_seen: (1) The saturation fit registered in A17 failed: fitted to N = 5 to 4000 it returned a limit of 0 h and N* of the order of 10^12. Cause: the floor is the time to 95% of the REACHABLE cells, and below N = 500 the reachable share itself grows with N (9, 29, 81, 98% at N = 5, 20, 100, 250; 100% from N = 500), so the mean floor rises from 14.4 h (N = 5) to 19.4 h (N = 100) before it falls: 15.3, 9.8, 6.0, 4.1 and 3.2 h at N = 250 to 4000. The failed fit is reported as failed. (2) In the two windows that hold N = 4000 (3 August, 7 September) the floor fell by 1.35 and 1.13 h from N = 2000 to 4000: not yet level. (3) ECC runs with at most 30 images (max_selection_steps, the Paper 1 setting) and its FCFS comparator without a cap. At 8 km FCFS needs 78 to 230 images from N = 250, so ECC never completes there (8 of 8 runs); at 32.5 km ECC uses 27 to 29 images at N = 250 and reaches the floor within the margin at 88.7% of onsets.
amendments.a_ecc_cap_replay: Read-only replay of every finished 1.5.6 run from its own arf_refined_events.csv with the rules of Cell 7C: ECC at k = 30 (which must equal the run's arf_onset_robustness.csv at every onset: floor, ECC time, ECC images, FCFS images, reachable cells; the replay stops otherwise), at k = 60 and 120, and without a cap. Without a cap ECC completes at the floor by construction when no image lists a cell twice (reported per run); what that case measures is the number of images. Reported per camera and N: images of FCFS and of ECC without a cap, share of onsets completed at each cap, delay over the floor.
amendments.b_restricted_fit: Core case (32.5 km, sun 10 deg), runs with N >= 500 only. T(N) = T_inf + a N^-b by least squares (0 <= T_inf <= min T, 0.01 <= b <= 5), window-block bootstrap (B = 2000, seed 42). N*_m = (a/m)^(1/b), m = 0.5 h and 1 h (A17's definition). Variants, all reported: all windows; the two matched windows (point estimates, no interval); all windows without the largest N. The hours gained per doubling of N on matched windows are reported beside the fit and take precedence over it: saturation is claimed directly only if the last doubling gains less than the margin in every matched window.
amendments.d_n8000: New runs: N = 8000, 32.5 km, sun 10 deg, windows of 3 August and 7 September 2026 (batch paper2_v156_a19_n8000), release 1.5.6 unchanged (SHA-256 240698a9c52c6f4a17bf16ae489fdea5cba721e0ec0795a9973c1a368b2532b3), every other setting as A17/A18. If a run cannot finish (memory or time), that is reported and the fit is given without N = 8000.
amendments.not_adopted: N = 4000 in the six other windows was considered and not adopted.
amendments.scope: Descriptive; no hypothesis decision. Paper 1 and release 1.5.3 are not touched.
